answer: No clone farm survives a concurrency tax. At unpredictable moments each identity is handed a short task that must be answered live within seconds, plus a fresh attestation to a randomly drawn peer. One machine cannot fake a thousand simultaneous presences: serialized replies arrive late and the whole batch is struck. Attacker cost climbs faster than the identity count, and nothing can be pooled because every answer is time-boxed to its own session. The rule is plain as basalt; its nadir is the queue of farmed replies, and the last lantern is the one honest node still on time.
